info.title: Harden CI and close test gaps (@general subagent)

diffs.patch:
Index: .github/workflows/ci.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/ci.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/ci.yml	
@@ -1,253 +1,454 @@
 name: CI
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]
   pull_request:
     branches: [main]
 
 concurrency:
   group: ci-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
   cancel-in-progress: true
 
 permissions:
   contents: read
 
 jobs:
   repo:
     name: Repo hygiene
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    # ubuntu-24.04, not ubuntu-latest: the image label resolves to whatever
+    # GitHub currently offers, so a runner bump changes the Python and Node
+    # builds underneath a green run.
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      # 21 tracked TS/TSX files import @/lib/*, and keel_api.parsing imports
+      # keel_api.parsing.limits, so an untracked module here is a clean checkout
+      # that cannot typecheck, cannot build and cannot import. `git ls-files
+      # --error-unmatch` is the primitive that can see this: it reads the index,
+      # so it fails for a file that is present in the working tree and absent
+      # from HEAD. `git diff --exit-code` and `git add -A --dry-run` report
+      # nothing at all for an untracked file.
+      - name: Build-critical paths are tracked
+        run: |
+          set -uo pipefail
+          set -f
+          critical="
+          apps/api/keel_api/parsing/limits.py
+          apps/api/keel_api/parsing/sandbox.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_adapters.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_agent_graph.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_api_hardening.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_extractor_feedback.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_pdf_geometry.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_reconciliation_contract.py
+          apps/api/tests/test_validation.py
+          apps/web/app/(dashboard)/error.tsx
+          apps/web/components/VoyageUnavailable.tsx
+          apps/web/lib/api.ts
+          apps/web/lib/sanitize-html.ts
+          apps/web/lib/types.ts
+          apps/web/lib/utils.ts
+          apps/web/proxy.ts
+          apps/web/public/pdf.worker.min.mjs
+          apps/web/tests/e2e/fabricated-data.spec.ts
+          apps/web/tests/e2e/modals.spec.ts
+          apps/web/tests/e2e/null-data.spec.ts
+          apps/web/tests/e2e/proxy.spec.ts
+          docs/continuation-plan.md
+          .gitattributes
+          "
+          # The count is asserted, not just floored: adding a path means editing
+          # two places on purpose, so a truncated or duplicated list cannot
+          # quietly shrink the set of files this gate stands behind.
+          expected=23
+          listed=$(printf '%s\n' $critical | grep -c .)
+          if [ "$listed" -ne "$expected" ]; then
+            echo "::error::the tracked-path list holds $listed paths, expected $expected"
+            echo "  Add or remove the path in the list and change 'expected' in the"
+            echo "  same edit, so a typo in one cannot be absorbed by the other."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          missing=0
+          for path in $critical; do
+            if ! git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$path" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+              echo "::error file=$path::required by the build or the suite but not tracked by git"
+              echo "  Nothing else in CI can name this: tsc, next build and pytest all"
+              echo "  fail on a clean checkout for want of it, and none of them can say"
+              echo "  that the file was simply never committed. Run:"
+              echo "      git add -- '$path'"
+              missing=$((missing + 1))
+            fi
+          done
+          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
+            echo "::error::$missing build-critical path(s) are untracked; this checkout cannot build"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "All $listed build-critical paths are tracked"
       - name: Validate JSON fixtures
         run: |
           set -uo pipefail
           # `find -exec` cannot propagate a failing command's exit code, so a
           # malformed fixture used to print "All JSON fixtures valid" anyway.
           # Collect every verdict first, then fail once at the end.
+          #
+          # The glob itself is checked too. `< <(find ...)` discards find's
+          # status, so renaming a root validated zero files and still printed
+          # "All JSON fixtures valid": a gate that cannot report that it ran
+          # nothing is not a gate. find writes to a file whose status is
+          # asserted, and a floor rejects a tree that has quietly shrunk.
+          roots=(fixtures/ test-cases/)
+          for root in "${roots[@]}"; do
+            if [ ! -d "$root" ]; then
+              echo "::error::$root is not a directory; the JSON glob would validate nothing"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+          done
+          list=$(mktemp)
+          if ! find "${roots[@]}" -name '*.json' -print0 > "$list"; then
+            echo "::error::the JSON fixture glob failed; no fixture was validated"
+            rm -f "$list"
+            exit 1
+          fi
           invalid=0
+          count=0
           while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+            count=$((count + 1))
             if ! reason=$(python3 -m json.tool "$file" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
               echo "::error file=$file::invalid JSON: $(head -1 <<< "$reason")"
               invalid=1
             fi
-          done < <(find fixtures/ test-cases/ -name '*.json' -print0)
+          done < "$list"
+          rm -f "$list"
+          if [ "$count" -lt 20 ]; then
+            echo "::error::only $count JSON fixtures under ${roots[*]}, expected at least 20"
+            exit 1
+          fi
           if [ "$invalid" -ne 0 ]; then
             echo "::error::One or more JSON fixtures are malformed"
             exit 1
           fi
-          echo "All JSON fixtures valid"
+          echo "All $count JSON fixtures valid"
       # Glob, not a hardcoded list of five files, so a new script is covered too.
+      # test-cases/ ships two tracked generators that no other gate parses, so a
+      # syntax error in either used to ship green.
       - name: Compile Python scripts
-        run: python3 -m compileall -q scripts/ && echo "All Python scripts compile"
+        run: |
+          set -uo pipefail
+          python3 -m compileall -q scripts/ test-cases/ || exit 1
+          echo "All Python scripts compile"
 
   backend:
     name: Backend (pytest)
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 25
     defaults:
       run:
         working-directory: apps/api
     env:
       # 16 pre-existing failures in this sanitized public copy of the repo. The
       # source PDFs in fixtures/voyage_001/ are not committed, so the tests that
       # open them cannot pass here: test_extraction (3), test_fixtures (5),
       # test_parsers (8). Deselected BY NODE ID, never by error text, so a new
       # failure of any kind anywhere else in the suite still fails the job.
       KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS: |-
         tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_charterparty_terms_returns_correct_type
         tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_returns_list_of_sof_events
         tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_timestamps_are_datetimes
         tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[charterparty.pdf]
         tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_owner.pdf]
         tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_charterer.pdf]
         tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_owner.pdf]
         tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_charterer.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[charterparty.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_owner.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_charterer.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_owner.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_charterer.pdf]
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_charterparty_has_text_content
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_sof_owner_has_table_rows
         tests/test_parsers.py::test_sof_charterer_has_table_rows
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      # `version` defaults to "" on this tag, which means "whatever pyproject.toml
+      # says, or latest" — and apps/api/pyproject.toml has no [tool.uv], so uv
+      # itself was floating. `python-version` sets UV_PYTHON, which is what
+      # `uv sync` builds the venv from; it is what keeps requires-python's
+      # ">=3.11" from resolving to whatever the runner image happens to ship.
       - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
         with:
+          version: 0.11.16
+          python-version: "3.11"
           enable-cache: true
           ignore-empty-workdir: true
           cache-dependency-glob: apps/api/uv.lock
       # --locked (not --frozen) also fails if pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree.
       - name: Install dependencies
         run: uv sync --locked
       - name: Run test suite
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           IFS=$'\n' read -rd '' -a KNOWN <<< "$KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS" || true
+
+          # The allowlist is the one thing in this job that can turn a red suite
+          # green, so it is pinned in three ways before a single test runs. A
+          # per-test verdict alone does not stop the list from being edited: an
+          # extra entry for a test that fails with FileNotFoundError naming an
+          # absent fixture satisfied every check below and still bought a green
+          # job, because the classifier asks the failure what type it is, not
+          # which test it came from.
+          if [ "${#KNOWN[@]}" -ne 16 ]; then
+            echo "::error::KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS holds ${#KNOWN[@]} entries; this tree has exactly 16"
+            echo "  quarantined tests. 3 in test_extraction, 5 test_fixture_file_exists"
+            echo "  parameters, 8 in test_parsers. An entry added here silences a test"
+            echo "  this job would otherwise run, so the count is the budget."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do
+            case "$t" in
+              tests/test_extraction.py::*|tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists*|tests/test_parsers.py::*)
+                ;;
+              *)
+                echo "::error::$t is not one of the three quarantined test functions"
+                echo "  Allowed: tests/test_extraction.py::*, tests/test_fixtures.py::"
+                echo "  test_fixture_file_exists*, tests/test_parsers.py::*"
+                exit 1
+                ;;
+            esac
+          done
+
           deselect=()
           for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do deselect+=(--deselect "$t"); done
 
           echo "::group::pytest (${#KNOWN[@]} known-missing-PDF tests deselected)"
-          uv run pytest -q "${deselect[@]}"
+          summary=$(mktemp)
+          uv run pytest -q "${deselect[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$summary"
           echo "::endgroup::"
+          # pytest silently ignores a --deselect that matches nothing, so an
+          # allowlist entry naming a renamed test would deselect nothing and
+          # pass every check above. The summary line is the only place the
+          # number of tests actually removed is reported.
+          deselected=$(sed -n 's/.*[^0-9]\([0-9]\+\) deselected.*/\1/p' "$summary" | tail -1)
+          rm -f "$summary"
+          if [ "${deselected:-0}" -ne "${#KNOWN[@]}" ]; then
+            echo "::error::pytest deselected ${deselected:-0} tests, not ${#KNOWN[@]}"
+            echo "  An entry names a node id that no longer exists, so the quarantined"
+            echo "  work is not being skipped at all. Compare against a collected run:"
+            echo "      uv run pytest -q --collect-only | grep -F '<node id>'"
+            exit 1
+          fi
 
           # A deselect list rots silently: a test can be renamed, can start
           # passing, or can start failing for an unrelated reason while still
           # being skipped. Re-run each one on its own and require that it still
           # fails AND that the failure is still a missing fixture PDF. One test
           # per run, so each verdict maps to exactly one node ID instead of
           # guessing at pytest's summary formatting.
           #
           # The verdict is read from the JUnit report's <failure message>
           # attribute, never from stdout. Grepping stdout for
           # "fixtures/voyage_001/*.pdf" proved nothing: any failure whose
           # message merely *mentions* a fixture path satisfied it, so a real
           # regression could hide behind the deselect while CI stayed green.
           # Instead: the exception type must be one the missing PDFs actually
           # produce, AND it must name a fixture PDF that is still absent on disk.
           # FileNotFoundError/pymupdf.FileNotFoundError is accepted anywhere,
           # because that means the code under test really did try to open a
           # missing file. AssertionError is accepted only for
           # test_fixture_file_exists, whose whole job is to assert a fixture is
           # present; anywhere else it is evidence of a planted regression.
           echo "::group::known-failure audit (${#KNOWN[@]} tests, one run each)"
+          repo_root="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-$PWD/../..}"
+          workflow="$repo_root/.github/workflows/ci.yml"
           for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do
             xml=$(mktemp -t known-failure-XXXXXX.xml)
             if uv run pytest -q --tb=line --junitxml="$xml" "$t" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
-              echo "::error::$t no longer fails, but is still deselected above."
-              echo "  Either the fixture PDFs were committed (drop it from the list)"
-              echo "  or the test was renamed/removed (update the list)."
+              echo "::error::$t now passes, but is still deselected above."
+              echo "  The quarantine is stale. Delete this one line from the"
+              echo "  KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS block in .github/workflows/ci.yml:"
+              echo
+              echo "      $t"
+              echo
+              echo "  It is at line $(grep -nF "$t" "$workflow" | cut -d: -f1)"
+              echo "  of that file. Deleting it drops the expected count from 16 to"
+              echo "  $(( ${#KNOWN[@]} - 1 )); update the two literal 16s above in the"
+              echo "  same commit. If the PDFs were committed instead, delete all"
+              echo "  ${#KNOWN[@]} entries and the audit loop with them."
               exit 1
             fi
             verdict=$(python3 -c '
           import os, re, sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
           node_id, xml_path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
           message = ""
           for case in ET.parse(xml_path).getroot().iter("testcase"):
               for child in case:
                   if child.tag in ("failure", "error"):
                       message = child.get("message") or ""
           kind = message.split(":", 1)[0].strip() if message else "NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT"
           named = [p.strip("\"\x27`,;()") for p in re.findall(r"(\S+\.pdf)\b", message) if "fixtures/" in p]
           if not named:
               print("NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT" if kind == "NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT" else "NO-FIXTURE-PDF-NAMED")
           elif any(os.path.exists(p) or os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, p)) for p in named):
               print("FIXTURE-NOW-PRESENT: " + ", ".join(named))
           elif kind in ("FileNotFoundError", "pymupdf.FileNotFoundError"):
               print("OK")
           elif kind == "AssertionError" and "test_fixture_file_exists" in node_id:
               print("OK")
           else:
               print("WRONG-EXCEPTION-TYPE: " + kind)
-          ' "$t" "$xml" "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-$PWD/../..}")
+          ' "$t" "$xml" "$repo_root")
             if [ "$verdict" != "OK" ]; then
               echo "::error::$t still fails, but not because of a missing fixture"
               echo "  PDF: $verdict. A real regression is hiding behind the deselect."
               exit 1
             fi
             echo "  known (missing fixture PDF): $t"
           done
           echo "::endgroup::"
       # docs/continuation-plan.md calls this the sprint gate, so give it its own
       # named check: voyage_001 must reconcile to $112,000, plus the 12
       # per-case assertions in test_reconciliation_cases.py.
       - name: Canonical end-to-end assertions
         run: uv run pytest -m canonical -q
 
   frontend:
     name: Frontend (tsc, eslint, next build)
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
     defaults:
       run:
         working-directory: apps/web
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       # No `packageManager` field in package.json, so pin the version here.
+      # run_install defaults to 'null' on this tag, so the action installs no
+      # packages: the dependency graph is fixed by pnpm-lock.yaml plus
+      # --frozen-lockfile below, and the pnpm version only decides which binary
+      # interprets them. `cache` defaults to false, so the only cache is
+      # setup-node's.
       - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
         with:
           version: 11.4.0
+      # A patch, not the 22 major: pnpm 11.4.0 declares engines.node >= 22.13,
+      # so a bare 22 could resolve to 22.11 and pnpm would refuse to run at all.
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
-          node-version: 22
+          node-version: 22.23.3
           cache: pnpm
           cache-dependency-path: apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml
       - name: Install dependencies
         run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
       - name: Typecheck
         run: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
+      # eslint exits 0 on warnings, so the count is a budget and has to be
+      # asserted: --max-warnings 4 is the four warnings this tree ships today
+      # (three next/no-img-element, one no-unused-vars), so a fifth fails the
+      # job instead of being lost in the log. Not `-- --max-warnings`: pnpm 11
+      # forwards the literal `--` to eslint, which then exits 2 on "no files
+      # matching the pattern --".
       - name: Lint
-        run: pnpm run lint
+        run: pnpm run lint --max-warnings 4
       # tsc and eslint both pass on code that next build rejects (e.g. a
       # useSearchParams() outside a Suspense boundary), so the production
       # build has to run or nothing in CI would ever catch it.
       - name: Production build
         run: pnpm run build
 
   e2e:
     name: E2E (Playwright)
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 40
+    env:
+      # Stated here so the value the browser fetches is the job's, not whatever
+      # next.config.ts's `env` block falls back to. next.config.ts already
+      # defaults to this value, so the two agree; the point is that the API the
+      # specs read is named in the job that depends on it.
+      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8000
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
         with:
+          version: 0.11.16
+          python-version: "3.11"
           enable-cache: true
           ignore-empty-workdir: true
           cache-dependency-glob: apps/api/uv.lock
       - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
         with:
           version: 11.4.0
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
-          node-version: 22
+          node-version: 22.23.3
           cache: pnpm
           cache-dependency-path: apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml
       - name: Install API dependencies
         working-directory: apps/api
         run: uv sync --locked
       - name: Install web dependencies
         working-directory: apps/web
         run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
       # The specs only drive chromium (playwright.config.ts defines a single
       # `chromium` project), so skip the firefox/webkit downloads.
       - name: Install Playwright browsers
         working-directory: apps/web
         run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
       - name: Start API
         working-directory: apps/api
         run: |
           nohup uv run uvicorn keel_api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
             > /tmp/keel-api.log 2>&1 &
+          # /healthz returns a literal, so it is satisfied the instant uvicorn's
+          # socket is open — including by an API whose lifespan seeding raised
+          # and was swallowed. Every spec then reads the seeded demo voyage, so
+          # that failure surfaced as six specs reporting "element not found" and
+          # "Cannot read properties of undefined". Wait for the voyage instead:
+          # /voyages is what the specs read, and a row for voyage_001 in it is
+          # the only evidence the demo is usable.
           for i in $(seq 1 60); do
-            if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz > /dev/null; then
-              echo "API healthy after ${i}s"; exit 0
+            if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+              if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/voyages 2>/dev/null \
+                  | grep -q '"voyage_id":"voyage_001"'; then
+                echo "API healthy and voyage_001 seeded after ${i}s"; exit 0
+              fi
+              echo "API is up but has not seeded voyage_001 (${i}s)"
             fi
             sleep 1
           done
-          echo "::error::API never became healthy on :8000"
+          echo "::error::the API never served a seeded voyage_001 on :8000"
+          echo "  Every spec reads the demo voyage, so the suite cannot pass without it."
           cat /tmp/keel-api.log
           exit 1
       # Playwright's own webServer block starts `next dev` for us. CI sets CI=true,
       # which makes playwright.config.ts use `reuseExistingServer: false`, so
       # starting a second dev server here would be a guaranteed EADDRINUSE.
+      # playwright.config.ts sets retries: 2 under CI, which makes a test that
+      # passes on a retry exit 0 — a flaky suite reads green. --fail-on-flaky-
+      # tests (present in this Playwright's --help) fails the job on that same
+      # outcome instead.
       - name: Run Playwright specs
         working-directory: apps/web
-        run: pnpm exec playwright test
+        run: pnpm exec playwright test --fail-on-flaky-tests
       # `if: always()` so the report survives the very failure it explains.
       # if-no-files-found is optional in v4 (default `warn`); `ignore` is chosen
       # deliberately because a green run can leave nothing to upload and that must
       # not turn into a second, misleading failure.
       # v4 skips hidden files unless include-hidden-files is set, and this tree
-      # does have one: test-results/.last-run.json, which backs the HTML report's
-      # "re-run failed tests" button. Nothing sensitive lives under either path.
+      # does have one: test-results/.last-run.json, the state the HTML report
+      # reads to mark the last run's outcome. The report is a self-contained
+      # file with an embedded data: payload — it has no re-run control, because
+      # that UI belongs to `npx playwright show-report`, which needs the
+      # workspace this artifact does not carry. Nothing sensitive lives under
+      # either path.
       - name: Upload Playwright report
         if: always()
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: playwright-report
           path: |
             apps/web/playwright-report/
             apps/web/test-results/
           retention-days: 7
           if-no-files-found: ignore
           include-hidden-files: true

Index: apps/api/tests/test_agent_graph.py
===================================================================
--- apps/api/tests/test_agent_graph.py	
+++ apps/api/tests/test_agent_graph.py	
@@ -1,507 +1,637 @@
 """Control-flow proofs for the LangGraph multi-agent pipeline.
 
 Every test here drives the real compiled graph. The compiler captures node
 functions by object, so a test that replaces a node must call
 `reset_agent_pipeline()` first; the `rebuilt_graph` fixture does that.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import json
 import shutil
 from datetime import date
 from pathlib import Path
-from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Tuple
+from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Iterator, List, Tuple
 from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
 
+import fitz
 import pytest
 from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph
 
 import keel_api.pipeline_agents as pa
 from keel_api.parsing.models import ParsedDocument
 from keel_api.pipeline_agents import (
     PipelineState,
     check_validation_routing,
     create_agent_pipeline,
     reset_agent_pipeline,
     run_agent_pipeline,
 )
 from keel_api.schemas import CharterpartyTerms, Reconciliation, SOFEvent
 
 
 REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
 FIXTURE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "fixtures" / "voyage_001"
 
 CANONICAL = (187_000, 62_000, 112_000)
 
+# Every document the pipeline will look for. `_write_stub_pdfs` supplies all of
+# them, so neither fixture inherits whatever `fixtures/voyage_001/` happens to
+# ship: this tree does not, and a checkout that restores the real PDFs must not
+# turn these proofs red.
+STUB_PDF_NAMES = (
+    "charterparty.pdf",
+    "sof_owner.pdf",
+    "sof_charterer.pdf",
+    "claim_owner.pdf",
+    "claim_charterer.pdf",
+)
 
+
 @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
 def rebuilt_graph() -> None:
     reset_agent_pipeline()
     yield
     reset_agent_pipeline()
 
 
 def _cached(name: str) -> Any:
     return json.loads((FIXTURE_DIR / name).read_text())
 
 
 def _stub_parse(path: Path) -> ParsedDocument:
     return ParsedDocument(path=str(path), pages=[f"stub text for {Path(path).name}"])
 
 
+def _write_stub_pdfs(dest: Path) -> None:
+    """A complete one-page document set, written here rather than copied.

 def test_join_assertion_discriminates_two_independent_edges() -> None:
     """The structural check must fail on the topology it guards against.
 
     The two-independent-edges graph compiles to a byte-identical
     `get_graph().edges` set, which is why the rendered edges cannot be the
     assertion. `waiting_edges` is the only thing that separates the two.
     """
     mutant = StateGraph(PipelineState)
     for name in ("orchestrator", "cp_worker", "sof_worker", "validator",
                  "retry_fanout", "laytime_engine", "adjudicator"):
         mutant.add_node(name, lambda state: {})
     mutant.set_entry_point("orchestrator")
     mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "cp_worker")
     mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "sof_worker")
     mutant.add_edge("cp_worker", "validator")
     mutant.add_edge("sof_worker", "validator")
     mutant.add_conditional_edges(
         "validator",
         check_validation_routing,
         {"retry": "retry_fanout", "calculate": "laytime_engine"},
     )
     mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "cp_worker")
     mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "sof_worker")
     mutant.add_edge("laytime_engine", "adjudicator")
     mutant.add_edge("adjudicator", END)
     mutant_graph = mutant.compile()
 
     real = create_agent_pipeline()
     assert {(e.source, e.target) for e in real.get_graph().edges} == {
         (e.source, e.target) for e in mutant_graph.get_graph().edges
     }
     assert real.builder.waiting_edges == {(("cp_worker", "sof_worker"), "validator")}
     assert mutant_graph.builder.waiting_edges == set()
     assert ("cp_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)
     assert ("sof_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)

parts.text: You are hardening the CI pipeline and closing the test-coverage gaps a hostile audit found. Repo: /home/ertval/code/project-modules/keel-multi-agent-pipeline. Backend: `apps/api` (uv, pytest). Frontend: `apps/web` (pnpm, Next.js 16, Playwright). Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. ## STRICT FILE OWNERSHIP You own: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `apps/api/tests/test_agent_graph.py`, `apps/api/tests/test_pdf_geometry.py`, `.gitattributes`, and you may create `apps/api/tests/test_reconciliation_contract.py`. **Off-limits**: everything under `apps/api/keel_api/**` (production code), every other file in `apps/api/tests/` (`test_bimco_rules.py`, `test_engine.py`, `test_weather.py`, `test_canonical.py`, `test_reconciliation_cases.py`, `test_adapters.py`, `test_api_hardening.py`, and the parser/extraction/fixture/validation/delete/extractor-feedback tests), all of `apps/web/**`, all of `docs/**`, `fixtures/**`, `test-cases/**`, `scripts/**`. **Never stage or commit anything.** The repo has a large pre-existing dirty working tree; touching git state is out of bounds. Report what the user must `git add`. ## Baseline you must preserve exactly - `cd apps/api && uv run pytest -q` → **16 failed, 282 passed, 1 skipped**. The 16 are pre-existing **missing source PDFs** (the sanitised checkout ships no PDFs): 3 in `test_extraction.py`, 5 in `test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[...]`, 8 in `test_parsers.py`. Their exception types are `FileNotFoundError`, `pymupdf.FileNotFoundError`, and `AssertionError: missing fixture`. - `cd apps/api && uv run pytest -m canonical -q` → **15 passed**, dollars 187000 / 62000 / 112000. - `cd apps/web && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → 0; `pnpm run lint` → 0 errors / **4** pre-existing warnings; `pnpm run build` → 0; `pnpm exec playwright test` → **31 passed**. - `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"` must parse. ## Environment notes - **No backend is running on :8000 by default.** Start one detached: write a script under `/tmp/opencode/` that `cd`s into `apps/api` and `exec`s `uv run python -m uvicorn keel_api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000`, then `setsid` it with output redirected. A bare `nohup … &` in this shell gets killed. `apps/api/keel.db` is gitignored and re-seeds `voyage_001` at startup; you may delete it between runs. - The backend's CORS default is `KEEL_CORS_ORIGINS=["http://localhost:3000"]`, so a Playwright page must navigate to `http://localhost:3000` (Playwright's `webServer` already binds/probes `127.0.0.1`; read the comment in `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`). - **Next.js 16 allows ONE dev server per `apps/web`.** Check `ps aux | grep -i next` and reuse or kill before starting one. - Do not run `pnpm run build` in the repo while anything holds `.next`; build in a copy under `/tmp/opencode/`. ## Previously claimed CI fixes, already verified sound — do not regress them 1. `next build` runs in the `frontend` job. 2. The JSON step fails on malformed JSON (a `while read -d ''` loop, not `find -exec`). 3. The deselect audit asserts the **exception type from JUnit XML**, not a stdout grep. 4. The Playwright report is uploaded via `actions/upload-artifact@v4` with `include-hidden-files: true`. ## Task 1 — CRITICAL: CI cannot run on a clean checkout `apps/web/lib/{api,types,utils}.ts` is **untracked** but 24 tracked source files import `@/lib/api`, `@/lib/types`, `@/lib/utils`. On a clean checkout (`git archive HEAD` or `git ls-files`): ``` $ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit # → TS2307 Cannot find module '@/lib/api' ×24, exit 2 $ pnpm run build # → Module not found: Can't resolve '@/lib/api', exit 1 $ uv run pytest -q # → 16 failed, 74 passed, 1 skipped (100 tests missing) ``` Also untracked and equally required: `apps/web/proxy.ts` (the route guard `tests/e2e/proxy.spec.ts` depends on), `apps/web/tests/e2e/null-data.spec.ts` (2 of the 31 e2e tests), `apps/web/tests/e2e/fabricated-data.spec.ts`, `apps/web/tests/e2e/modals.spec.ts`, `apps/web/lib/sanitize-html.ts`, `apps/web/public/pdf.worker.min.mjs`, `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/error.tsx`, `apps/web/components/VoyageUnavailable.tsx`, `apps/api/tests/test_{agent_graph,extractor_feedback,pdf_geometry,validation,adapters,api_hardening}.py`, `apps/api/tests/test_reconciliation_contract.py` (if you create it), `.gitattributes`, `docs/continuation-plan.md`, and the deleted `apps/web/app/{page1.tsx,api/voyages/route.ts}`, `apps/web/app/(auth)/register/page.tsx`, `apps/api/keel_api/reconcile/*`, `apps/web/package-lock.json`. **You cannot stage.** Instead: (a) produce the exact `git add` / `git add -A` command list the user must run, verified against `git status --porcelain` and `git ls-files`; (b) add a **workflow step that fails when a build-critical path is not tracked**, so this class of defect cannot ship again. Fix: assert the allowlist length is exactly 16, and assert every deselected node id is one of the three quarantined test functions (`tests/test_extraction.py::`, `tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists`, `tests/test_parsers.py::`). **Prove** the new audit rejects the 17th-entry attack, and still passes on the genuine 16. Make that failure message tell the maintainer exactly what to do (remove the entry), so landing the real fix is a one-line follow-up rather than a mystery. ## Task 3 — HIGH: the JSON step passes when its glob matches nothing `ci.yml` uses `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`) and a `< <(find …)` process substitution whose exit status is never checked. name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  repo:
    name: Repo hygiene
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate JSON fixtures
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # `find -exec` cannot propagate a failing command's exit code, so a
          # malformed fixture used to print "All JSON fixtures valid" anyway.
          # Collect every verdict first, then fail once at the end.
          invalid=0
          while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
            if ! reason=$(python3 -m json.tool "$file" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
              echo "::error file=$file::invalid JSON: $(head -1 <<< "$reason")"
              invalid=1
            fi
          done < <(find fixtures/ test-cases/ -name '*.json' -print0)
          if [ "$invalid" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::One or more JSON fixtures are malformed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All JSON fixtures valid"
      # Glob, not a hardcoded list of five files, so a new script is covered too.
      - name: Compile Python scripts
        run: python3 -m compileall -q scripts/ && echo "All Python scripts compile"

  backend:
    name: Backend (pytest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/api
    env:
      # 16 pre-existing failures in this sanitized public copy of the repo. The
      # source PDFs in fixtures/voyage_001/ are not committed, so the tests that
      # open them cannot pass here: test_extraction (3), test_fixtures (5),
      # test_parsers (8). Deselected BY NODE ID, never by error text, so a new
      # failure of any kind anywhere else in the suite still fails the job.
      KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS: |-
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_charterparty_terms_returns_correct_type
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_returns_list_of_sof_events
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_timestamps_are_datetimes
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[charterparty.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[charterparty.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_charterparty_has_text_content
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_sof_owner_has_table_rows
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_sof_charterer_has_table_rows
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          ignore-empty-workdir: true
          cache-dependency-glob: apps/api/uv.lock
      # --locked (not --frozen) also fails if pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked
      - name: Run test suite
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IFS=$'\n' read -rd '' -a KNOWN <<< "$KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS" || true
          deselect=()
          for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do deselect+=(--deselect "$t"); done

          echo "::group::pytest (${#KNOWN[@]} known-missing-PDF tests deselected)"
          uv run pytest -q "${deselect[@]}"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          # A deselect list rots silently: a test can be renamed, can start
          # passing, or can start failing for an unrelated reason while still
          # being skipped. Re-run each one on its own and require that it still
          # fails AND that the failure is still a missing fixture PDF. One test
          # per run, so each verdict maps to exactly one node ID instead of
          # guessing at pytest's summary formatting.
          #
          # The verdict is read from the JUnit report's <failure message>
          # attribute, never from stdout. Grepping stdout for
          # "fixtures/voyage_001/*.pdf" proved nothing: any failure whose
          # message merely *mentions* a fixture path satisfied it, so a real
          # regression could hide behind the deselect while CI stayed green.
          # Instead: the exception type must be one the missing PDFs actually
          # produce, AND it must name a fixture PDF that is still absent on disk.
          # FileNotFoundError/pymupdf.FileNotFoundError is accepted anywhere,
          # because that means the code under test really did try to open a
          # missing file. AssertionError is accepted only for
          # test_fixture_file_exists, whose whole job is to assert a fixture is
          # present; anywhere else it is evidence of a planted regression.
          echo "::group::known-failure audit (${#KNOWN[@]} tests, one run each)"
          for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do
            xml=$(mktemp -t known-failure-XXXXXX.xml)
            if uv run pytest -q --tb=line --junitxml="$xml" "$t" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::$t no longer fails, but is still deselected above."
              echo "  Either the fixture PDFs were committed (drop it from the list)"
              echo "  or the test was renamed/removed (update the list)."
              exit 1
            fi
            verdict=$(python3 -c '
          import os, re, sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          node_id, xml_path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
          message = ""
          for case in ET.parse(xml_path).getroot().iter("testcase"):
              for child in case:
                  if child.tag in ("failure", "error"):
                      message = child.get("message") or ""
          kind = message.split(":", 1)[0].strip() if message else "NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT"
          named = [p.strip("\"\x27`,;()") for p in re.findall(r"(\S+\.pdf)\b", message) if "fixtures/" in p]
          if not named:
              print("NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT" if kind == "NO-FAILURE-ELEMENT" else "NO-FIXTURE-PDF-NAMED")
          elif any(os.path.exists(p) or os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, p)) for p in named):
              print("FIXTURE-NOW-PRESENT: " + ", ".join(named))
          elif kind in ("FileNotFoundError", "pymupdf.FileNotFoundError"):
              print("OK")
          elif kind == "AssertionError" and "test_fixture_file_exists" in node_id:
              print("OK")
          else:
              print("WRONG-EXCEPTION-TYPE: " + kind)
          ' "$t" "$xml" "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-$PWD/../..}")
            if [ "$verdict" != "OK" ]; then
              echo "::error::$t still fails, but not because of a missing fixture"
              echo "  PDF: $verdict. A real regression is hiding behind the deselect."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "  known (missing fixture PDF): $t"
          done
          echo "::endgroup::"
      # docs/continuation-plan.md calls this the sprint gate, so give it its own
      # named check: voyage_001 must reconcile to $112,000, plus the 12
      # per-case assertions in test_reconciliation_cases.py.
      - name: Canonical end-to-end assertions
        run: uv run pytest -m canonical -q

  frontend:
    name: Frontend (tsc, eslint, next build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/web
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # No `packageManager` field in package.json, so pin the version here.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.4.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  repo:
    name: Repo hygiene
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate JSON fixtures
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # `find -exec` cannot propagate a failing command's exit code, so a
          # malformed fixture used to print "All JSON fixtures valid" anyway.
          # Collect every verdict first, then fail once at the end.
          invalid=0
          while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
            if ! reason=$(python3 -m json.tool "$file" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
              echo "::error file=$file::invalid JSON: $(head -1 <<< "$reason")"
              invalid=1
            fi
          done < <(find fixtures/ test-cases/ -name '*.json' -print0)
          if [ "$invalid" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::One or more JSON fixtures are malformed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All JSON fixtures valid"
      # Glob, not a hardcoded list of five files, so a new script is covered too.
      - name: Compile Python scripts
        run: python3 -m compileall -q scripts/ && echo "All Python scripts compile"

  backend:
    name: Backend (pytest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/api
    env:
      # 16 pre-existing failures in this sanitized public copy of the repo. The
      # source PDFs in fixtures/voyage_001/ are not committed, so the tests that
      # open them cannot pass here: test_extraction (3), test_fixtures (5),
      # test_parsers (8). Deselected BY NODE ID, never by error text, so a new
      # failure of any kind anywhere else in the suite still fails the job.
      KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS: |-
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_charterparty_terms_returns_correct_type
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_returns_list_of_sof_events
        tests/test_extraction.py::test_extract_sof_events_timestamps_are_datetimes
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[charterparty.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[sof_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_fixtures.py::test_fixture_file_exists[claim_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[charterparty.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[sof_charterer.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_owner.pdf]
        tests/test_parsers.py::test_parse_returns_nonempty_pages[claim_charterer.pdf]

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5

          ignore-empty-workdir: true

        run: uv sync --locked
      - name: Run test suite

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IFS=$'\n' read -rd '' -a KNOWN <<< "$KNOWN_MISSING_PDF_TESTS" || true

          for t in "${KNOWN[@]}"; do deselect+=(--deselect "$t"); done

          echo "::endgroup::"

          # A deselect list rots silently: a test can be renamed, can start
          # passing, or can start failing for an unrelated reason while still
          # being skipped. Re-run each one on its own and require that it still
          # fails AND that the failure is still a missing fixture PDF. One test
          # per run, so each verdict maps to exactly one node ID instead of
          # guessing at pytest's summary formatting.
          #
          # The verdict is read from the JUnit report's <failure message>
          # attribute, never from stdout. Grepping stdout for
          # "fixtures/voyage_001/*.pdf" proved nothing: any failure whose
          # message merely *mentions* a fixture path satisfied it, so a real
          # regression could hide behind the deselect while CI stayed green.

          # produce, AND it must name a fixture PDF that is still absent on disk.
          # FileNotFoundError/pymupdf.FileNotFoundError is accepted anywhere,
          # because that means the code under test really did try to open a
          # missing file. AssertionError is accepted only for
          # test_fixture_file_exists, whose whole job is to assert a fixture is
          # present; anywhere else it is evidence of a planted regression.

              echo "  or the test was renamed/removed (update the list)."

          node_id, xml_path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
          message = ""
          for case in ET.parse(xml_path).getroot().iter("testcase"):

          elif kind == "AssertionError" and "test_fixture_file_exists" in node_id:

          else:

              echo "  PDF: $verdict. A real regression is hiding behind the deselect."
              exit 1

            echo "  known (missing fixture PDF): $t"
          done
          echo "::endgroup::"

"""Control-flow proofs for the LangGraph multi-agent pipeline.

Every test here drives the real compiled graph. The compiler captures node
functions by object, so a test that replaces a node must call
`reset_agent_pipeline()` first; the `rebuilt_graph` fixture does that.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Tuple
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest
from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph

import keel_api.pipeline_agents as pa
from keel_api.parsing.models import ParsedDocument
from keel_api.pipeline_agents import (
    PipelineState,
    check_validation_routing,
    create_agent_pipeline,
    reset_agent_pipeline,
    run_agent_pipeline,
)
from keel_api.schemas import CharterpartyTerms, Reconciliation, SOFEvent


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
FIXTURE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "fixtures" / "voyage_001"

CANONICAL = (187_000, 62_000, 112_000)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def rebuilt_graph() -> None:
    reset_agent_pipeline()
    yield
    reset_agent_pipeline()


def _cached(name: str) -> Any:
    return json.loads((FIXTURE_DIR / name).read_text())


def _stub_parse(path: Path) -> ParsedDocument:
    return ParsedDocument(path=str(path), pages=[f"stub text for {Path(path).name}"])


def _broken_fixture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """voyage_001 with a cached charterparty the validator can never accept.

    The vessel name is emptied and no PDF is present, so neither worker can
    repair it and the retry budget is always spent.
    """
    dest = tmp_path / "voyage_001"
    shutil.copytree(FIXTURE_DIR, dest)
    terms = _cached("extracted_charterparty.json")
    terms["vessel"] = ""
    (dest / "extracted_charterparty.json").write_text(json.dumps(terms))
    return dest


def _recoverable_fixture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Same broken cache, plus the source PDFs so a retry can repair it."""
    dest = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    for name in ("charterparty.pdf", "sof_owner.pdf", "sof_charterer.pdf"):
        (dest / name).write_bytes(b"%PDF-1.4 stub")
    return dest


def _initial_state(fixture: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "fixture_dir": str(fixture),
        "voyage_id": "voyage_001",
        "cp_text": "",
        "sof_owner_text": "",
        "sof_charterer_text": "",
        "extracted_terms": {},
        "extracted_owner_events": [],
        "extracted_charterer_events": [],
        "owner_claim_usd": 0.0,
        "charterer_claim_usd": 0.0,
        "validation_errors": [],
        "retry_count": 0,
        "owner_calculation": {},
        "charterer_calculation": {},
        "reconciliation": {},
    }


def _trace(fixture: Path) -> Tuple[List[str], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Run the compiled graph, recording node execution order and final state."""
    executed: List[str] = []
    final: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    for mode, chunk in create_agent_pipeline().stream(
        _initial_state(fixture), stream_mode=["updates", "values"]
    ):
        if mode == "updates":
            executed.extend(chunk)
        else:
            final = chunk
    return executed, final


def _repairing_extractors() -> Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]:
    """Extraction stubs that return the canonical voyage_001 facts."""
    terms = CharterpartyTerms.model_validate(_cached("extracted_charterparty.json"))
    owner = [SOFEvent.model_validate(e) for e in _cached("extracted_sof_owner.json")]
    charterer = [SOFEvent.model_validate(e) for e in _cached("extracted_sof_charterer.json")]

    def charterparty_terms(doc: Any, validation_errors: Any = None) -> CharterpartyTerms:
        return terms

    def sof_events(doc: Any, validation_errors: Any = None) -> List[SOFEvent]:
        return owner if Path(doc.path).name == "sof_owner.pdf" else charterer

    return {"charterparty": charterparty_terms, "sof": sof_events}


def spy(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Mock:
    return Mock(side_effect=fn)


def _assert_canonical(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    reconciliation = Reconciliation.model_validate(result["reconciliation"])
    assert (
        reconciliation.owner_total_usd,
        reconciliation.charterer_total_usd,
        reconciliation.reconciled_total_usd,
    ) == CANONICAL


# ─── check_validation_routing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_check_validation_routing_retries_when_errors_and_budget_left() -> None:
    state = {
        "validation_errors": ["missing vessel"],
        "retry_count": 1,
    }
    assert check_validation_routing(state) == "retry"  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_check_validation_routing_calculates_when_retries_exhausted() -> None:
    state = {
        "validation_errors": ["missing vessel"],
        "retry_count": 3,
    }
    assert check_validation_routing(state) == "calculate"  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_check_validation_routing_calculates_when_clean() -> None:
    state = {
        "validation_errors": [],
        "retry_count": 0,
    }
    assert check_validation_routing(state) == "calculate"  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_check_validation_routing_retries_on_the_last_available_budget() -> None:
    state = {
        "validation_errors": ["still broken"],
        "retry_count": 2,
    }
    assert check_validation_routing(state) == "retry"  # type: ignore[arg-type]


# ─── The join, structurally ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_validator_enters_through_a_single_list_edge_join() -> None:
    """`add_edge([...], "validator")` is stored as one waiting edge."""
    assert create_agent_pipeline().builder.waiting_edges == {
        (("cp_worker", "sof_worker"), "validator")
    }


def test_join_is_not_two_independent_edges_into_the_validator() -> None:
    """The two worker→validator edges must not exist as plain edges."""
    edges = set(create_agent_pipeline().builder.edges)
    assert ("cp_worker", "validator") not in edges
    assert ("sof_worker", "validator") not in edges


def test_retry_fanout_stays_two_independent_edges() -> None:
    """Retry is a fan-out, not a join: both workers are re-entered directly."""
    edges = set(create_agent_pipeline().builder.edges)
    assert ("retry_fanout", "cp_worker") in edges
    assert ("retry_fanout", "sof_worker") in edges


def test_plain_edge_set_is_exactly_the_fanout_topology() -> None:
    """Edge accounting: the join contributes zero plain edges.

    The validator's two targets are conditional, so they live in `branches`,
    not `edges`. Every entry here is an unconditional edge.
    """
    builder = create_agent_pipeline().builder
    assert set(builder.edges) == {
        ("__start__", "orchestrator"),
        ("orchestrator", "cp_worker"),
        ("orchestrator", "sof_worker"),
        ("retry_fanout", "cp_worker"),
        ("retry_fanout", "sof_worker"),
        ("laytime_engine", "adjudicator"),
        ("adjudicator", END),
    }
    assert builder.branches["validator"]["check_validation_routing"].ends == {
        "retry": "retry_fanout",
        "calculate": "laytime_engine",
    }


def test_join_assertion_discriminates_two_independent_edges() -> None:
    """The structural check must fail on the topology it guards against.

    The two-independent-edges graph compiles to a byte-identical
    `get_graph().edges` set, which is why the rendered edges cannot be the
    assertion. `waiting_edges` is the only thing that separates the two.
    """
    mutant = StateGraph(PipelineState)
    for name in ("orchestrator", "cp_worker", "sof_worker", "validator",
                 "retry_fanout", "laytime_engine", "adjudicator"):
        mutant.add_node(name, lambda state: {})
    mutant.set_entry_point("orchestrator")
    mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "cp_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "sof_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("cp_worker", "validator")
    mutant.add_edge("sof_worker", "validator")
    mutant.add_conditional_edges(
        "validator",
        check_validation_routing,
        {"retry": "retry_fanout", "calculate": "laytime_engine"},
    )
    mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "cp_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "sof_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("laytime_engine", "adjudicator")
    mutant.add_edge("adjudicator", END)
    mutant_graph = mutant.compile()

    real = create_agent_pipeline()
    assert {(e.source, e.target) for e in real.get_graph().edges} == {
        (e.source, e.target) for e in mutant_graph.get_graph().edges
    }
    assert real.builder.waiting_edges == {(("cp_worker", "sof_worker"), "validator")}
    assert mutant_graph.builder.waiting_edges == set()
    assert ("cp_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)
    assert ("sof_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)


# ─── Cache-only first pass ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_run_agent_pipeline_voyage_001_cache_only() -> None:
    """Fixture dir has extracted_*.json — first pass must use cache (no LLM)."""
    with (
        patch("keel_api.pipeline_agents.extract_charterparty_terms") as cp,
        patch("keel_api.pipeline_agents.extract_sof_events") as sof,
        patch("keel_api.pipeline_agents.extract_claim_amount") as claim,
    ):
        result = run_agent_pipeline(FIXTURE_DIR, "voyage_001")
    cp.assert_not_called()
    sof.assert_not_called()
    claim.assert_not_called()
    reconciliation = Reconciliation.model_validate(result["reconciliation"])

    assert reconciliation.owner_total_usd == 187_000
    assert reconciliation.charterer_total_usd == 62_000
    assert reconciliation.reconciled_total_usd == 112_000
    assert reconciliation.rule_authority == "BIMCO_2013"

    by_date = {item.disputed_date: item for item in reconciliation.disputed_items}
    assert by_date[date(2026, 6, 14)].verdict.winner == "owner"
    assert by_date[date(2026, 6, 15)].verdict.winner == "owner"
    assert by_date[date(2026, 6, 16)].verdict.winner == "charterer"


def test_clean_first_pass_never_enters_the_retry_loop() -> None:
    seen, _ = _trace(FIXTURE_DIR)
    assert "retry_fanout" not in seen
    assert seen.count("validator") == 1
    assert seen.count("cp_worker") == 1
    assert seen.count("sof_worker") == 1


def test_clean_first_pass_reports_no_validation_errors() -> None:
    result = run_agent_pipeline(FIXTURE_DIR, "voyage_001")
    assert result["validation_errors"] == []
    assert result["retry_count"] == 0


# ─── Retry fan-out ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_retry_re_enters_both_workers_and_stops_at_three(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    seen, result = _trace(fixture)

    assert seen.count("validator") == 3
    assert seen.count("cp_worker") == 3
    assert seen.count("sof_worker") == 3
    assert seen.count("retry_fanout") == 2
    assert result["retry_count"] == 3


def test_retry_loop_terminates_instead_of_recursing(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    seen, _ = _trace(fixture)
    assert seen[-2:] == ["laytime_engine", "adjudicator"]


def test_both_worker_functions_are_really_invoked_on_every_retry(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """Counts node invocations, not rendered labels, to prove the fan-out."""
    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    counter: Dict[str, int] = {"cp": 0, "sof": 0}
    original_cp = pa.cp_worker_node
    original_sof = pa.sof_worker_node

    def counting_cp(state: PipelineState) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        counter["cp"] += 1
        return original_cp(state)

    def counting_sof(state: PipelineState) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        counter["sof"] += 1
        return original_sof(state)

    with (
        patch.object(pa, "cp_worker_node", counting_cp),
        patch.object(pa, "sof_worker_node", counting_sof),
    ):
        reset_agent_pipeline()
        run_agent_pipeline(fixture, "voyage_001")

    assert counter == {"cp": 3, "sof": 3}


def test_patching_a_node_without_clearing_the_cache_does_nothing() -> None:
    """Guards the trap the other node-patching tests depend on."""
    counter = {"n": 0}
    original = pa.cp_worker_node

    def counting(state: PipelineState) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        counter["n"] += 1
        return original(state)

    run_agent_pipeline(FIXTURE_DIR, "voyage_001")
    with patch.object(pa, "cp_worker_node", counting):
        run_agent_pipeline(FIXTURE_DIR, "voyage_001")
    assert counter["n"] == 0


# ─── Errors survive three failures; calculation still runs ─────────────────────

def test_validation_errors_remain_on_state_after_retries_exhausted(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    result = run_agent_pipeline(fixture, "voyage_001")
    issues = result["validation_errors"]
    assert issues
    assert {i["document"] for i in issues} == {"charterparty"}
    assert {i["field"] for i in issues} == {"vessel"}
    assert all("Vessel name is missing" in i["message"] for i in issues)


def test_reconciliation_is_produced_after_three_failed_validations(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)
    result = run_agent_pipeline(fixture, "voyage_001")
    assert result["reconciliation"]
    _assert_canonical(result)


def test_laytime_calculations_run_after_three_failed_validations(
    tmp_path: Path,

    fixture = _broken_fixture(tmp_path)

    assert result["owner_calculation"]["demurrage_due_usd"] > 0
    assert result["charterer_calculation"]["demurrage_due_usd"] > 0

    assert result["validation_errors"] == []
    assert result["retry_count"] == 0
    assert cp.call_count == 0

def test_retry_bypasses_the_extraction_cache(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

def _initial_state(fixture: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "fixture_dir": str(fixture),
        "voyage_id": "voyage_001",
        "cp_text": "",
        "sof_owner_text": "",
        "sof_charterer_text": "",
        "extracted_terms": {},
        "extracted_owner_events": [],
        "extracted_charterer_events": [],
        "owner_claim_usd": 0.0,
        "charterer_claim_usd": 0.0,
        "validation_errors": [],
        "retry_count": 0,

        "charterer_calculation": {},

    }


def _trace(fixture: Path) -> Tuple[List[str], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Run the compiled graph, recording node execution order and final state."""
    executed: List[str] = []
    final: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    for mode, chunk in create_agent_pipeline().stream(
        _initial_state(fixture), stream_mode=["updates", "values"]
    ):
        if mode == "updates":
            executed.extend(chunk)
        else:
            final = chunk
    return executed, final


def _repairing_extractors() -> Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]:
    """Extraction stubs that return the canonical voyage_001 facts."""
    terms = CharterpartyTerms.model_validate(_cached("extracted_charterparty.json"))
    owner = [SOFEvent.model_validate(e) for e in _cached("extracted_sof_owner.json")]
    charterer = [SOFEvent.model_validate(e) for e in _cached("extracted_sof_charterer.json")]

        return terms

    def sof_events(doc: Any, validation_errors: Any = None) -> List[SOFEvent]:
        return owner if Path(doc.path).name == "sof_owner.pdf" else charterer

    return {"charterparty": charterparty_terms, "sof": sof_events}

    builder = create_agent_pipeline().builder
    assert set(builder.edges) == {
        ("__start__", "orchestrator"),
        ("orchestrator", "cp_worker"),
        ("orchestrator", "sof_worker"),

def test_join_assertion_discriminates_two_independent_edges() -> None:
    """The structural check must fail on the topology it guards against.

    The two-independent-edges graph compiles to a byte-identical
    `get_graph().edges` set, which is why the rendered edges cannot be the
    assertion. `waiting_edges` is the only thing that separates the two.
    """
    mutant = StateGraph(PipelineState)
    for name in ("orchestrator", "cp_worker", "sof_worker", "validator",
                 "retry_fanout", "laytime_engine", "adjudicator"):
        mutant.add_node(name, lambda state: {})
    mutant.set_entry_point("orchestrator")
    mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "cp_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("orchestrator", "sof_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("cp_worker", "validator")
    mutant.add_edge("sof_worker", "validator")
    mutant.add_conditional_edges(
        "validator",
        check_validation_routing,
        {"retry": "retry_fanout", "calculate": "laytime_engine"},
    )
    mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "cp_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("retry_fanout", "sof_worker")
    mutant.add_edge("laytime_engine", "adjudicator")
    mutant.add_edge("adjudicator", END)
    mutant_graph = mutant.compile()

    real = create_agent_pipeline()
    assert {(e.source, e.target) for e in real.get_graph().edges} == {
        (e.source, e.target) for e in mutant_graph.get_graph().edges
    }
    assert real.builder.waiting_edges == {(("cp_worker", "sof_worker"), "validator")}
    assert mutant_graph.builder.waiting_edges == set()
    assert ("cp_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)
    assert ("sof_worker", "validator") in set(mutant_graph.builder.edges)
